title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
steps: 1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays. Two Tray — hear sound.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence. Two Tray — notice detail.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one aloud.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same. Two Tray — next action.

title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
goal: A worst-case story loses size when it gains a route.
steps: 1. Name Fear — Picture the feared ending in one line. Worst Case — feel support.
2. Build Exits — Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
3. Add Likely — Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely. Worst Case — add counterfact.
4. Climb Route — Move through the five steps once in your mind.
5. Act Now — Then take the first coping action available now. Worst Case — next action.

title: THE GREY DIAL
goal: Binary thinking hates a numbered dial.
steps: 1. Name Extremes — Name the two extremes your mind is using. Grey Dial — move slowly.
2. Build Scale — Build a 0–10 scale between them and say three real anchor points: 2, 5, and 8.
3. Place Today — Place today’s event where the evidence fits—not where the emotion shouts. Grey Dial — find evidence.
4. Choose Response — Choose a response matched to that exact setting. Grey Dial — next action.

steps: 1. Imagine Trusted — Imagine a trusted person bringing you the same facts. Borrow Their — loosen hands.

3. Remove Name — Now remove their name. Borrow Their — allow opposite.
4. Apply Page — Apply that page to yourself without adding a harsher clause. Borrow Their — next action.

title: THE RULE UNDER THE RULE
goal: A surface thought often works for a hidden constitution.
steps: 1. Picture Painful — Picture the painful thought. Rule Under — soften shoulders.
2. Ask Meaning — Ask, ‘If that were true, what would it mean about me, others, or life?’ Answer quickly, then ask the same question of the answer.
3. Continue Stable — Continue only until one stable rule repeats. Rule Under — pick action.
4. Box Rule — Box Rule Rule that rule.
5. Today — Today’s task is to inspect it, not obey it. Rule Under — next action.

title: THE SCHEMA CONTRABAND FILE
goal: Smuggle disconfirming reality past the old filter.
steps: 1. Capture — Catch one event your negative self-story would normally delete. Schema Contraband — hear sound.
2. Describe Happened — Say what happened, why it genuinely contradicts the old rule, and which convenient excuse the rule will use to dismiss it. Schema Contraband — allow opposite.
3. Sign — Sign the entry as usable evidence and reread it tomorrow once—no chanting. Schema Contraband — next action.

title: THE SKY DOES NOT BECOME THE WEATHER

2. Say Being — For each, say: ‘This is being noticed.’ Search for the noticing itself—its colour, age, or mood.
3. Rest Openness — If none can be found, rest with that openness for ten seconds. Sky Does — split duty.
4. Return Feeling — Return by feeling both feet. Sky Does — next action.

goal: Choose before distress turns choice into fog.
steps: 1. Prepare Five — Prepare five ten-minute diversions across different channels: hands, movement, sound, practical task, safe contact. Crisis Menu — widen gaze.
2. Select Option — During a spike, select the first available option without browsing for the perfect one. Crisis Menu — allow opposite.
3. Finish Interval — Finish the interval, reassess safety, then either return or choose support. Crisis Menu — next action.

title: DOES THE FEELING FIT THE FILE?

steps: 1. Separate Cards — Separate four cards: prompting event, meaning, verified evidence, actual present threat. Does Feeling — breathe naturally.
2. Compare Emotion — Compare the emotion’s intensity and duration with the fourth card.
3. Use Feeling — If they fit, use the feeling’s message. Does Feeling — name feeling.
4. Update Meaning — If they exceed it, regulate first and update the meaning. Does Feeling — next action.

title: REVERSE THE URGE, COMPLETELY
goal: When the emotion is unjustified, half-opposites do not retrain it.
steps: 1. Check Support — Verify that the facts do not support the action impulse. Reverse Urge — move slowly.
2. Speak Gently — Then perform its full safe opposite: approach instead of avoid, speak gently instead of attack, straighten instead of collapse, engage instead of hide. Reverse Urge — name feeling.
3. Match Posture — Match posture, words, and behaviour until the new signal is coherent. Reverse Urge — next action.

title: URGE IS NOT EMOTION
goal: Separate the weather from what it pushes you to do.
steps: 1. Name Emotion — Label the emotion in one word. Urge Emotion — widen gaze.
2. Hide Name — Name every behaviour it is urging—text, withdraw, shout, spend, hide, check.
3. Safe — Notice each SAFE, COSTLY, or UNCLEAR. Urge Emotion — name feeling.
4. Choose Safe — Select a low-risk move that respects the emotion without automatically enacting its favourite instruction. Urge Emotion — next action.

title: LET THE EMOTION FINISH ONE CHAPTER
goal: Interrupted feelings keep restarting the book.
steps: 1. Identify Chapter — Spot the current chapter only: sensation, meaning, action urge, or settling. Let Emotion — move slowly.
2. Permit — Permit the next natural chapter while withholding later ones.
3. Pause Meaning — If sensation is active, do not interpret; if meaning is clear, do not act yet. Let Emotion — name feeling.
4. Continue Genuine — Continue until a genuine settling marker—breath change, warmth, tears ending, posture release—appears. Let Emotion — next action.

3. Add Small — Add a small gesture while the memory is vivid. Install Capable — name sensation.
4. Release Gesture — Release, then use the gesture once to see whether the quality returns. Install Capable — next action.

title: STAMP WHERE THE DETAIL CAME FROM
goal: A memory matters without every detail carrying equal certainty.
steps: 1. Pick Detail — Choose one small memory detail; do not replay the event. Stamp Where — press feet.
2. Tag Source — Stamp it SENSED, INFERRED, LEARNED LATER, or UNSURE.
3. Rate Confidence — Give the detail a confidence word—high, medium, low, or unknown—based on its source rather than its emotional intensity. Stamp Where — allow opposite.
4. Keep Core — Picture one core fact that remains reliable and let the other detail keep its honest uncertainty. Stamp Where — next action.

4. Train — Train the opposite channel through embodiment. Install Counter — next action.

title: ERASE THE OBJECT, KEEP THE CONTACT
goal: Let focus outlive its original target.
steps: 1. Stabilise — Stabilise attention on one simple form. Erase Object — loosen hands.
2. Remove Name — Gradually remove its name, meaning, shape, and boundary in that order.
3. Attend Object — Preserve the ongoing sense of attending as the object loses definition. Erase Object — split duty.
4. Rest Briefly — Rest briefly with contact that no longer depends on a clear thing. Erase Object — next action.

steps: 1. Experience — Notice an experience before describing it. Find First — loosen hands.
2. Wait Moment — Wait for the moment ‘I,’ ‘mine,’ or ‘about me’ attaches.
3. Trace Addition — Trace that addition to a body sensation, image, or location. Find First — name sensation.
4. Observe Attachment — Observe the attachment without removing it.
5. Task — The task is detection, not metaphysical victory. Find First — next action.

title: THE FIVE-LAYER INSPECTION
goal: Identity may be wearing several visible coats.
steps: 1. Move Body — Move through body, energy, mind, intellect, and deep ease. Five Layer — soften shoulders.
2. Ask Change — At each layer ask what is present, what changes, and how it is known.
3. Keep All Layers — Do not discard any layer. Five Layer — notice detail.
4. Place Like — Place them like translucent sheets within awareness, then select the layer needed for practical action. Five Layer — next action.

title: THE WAKING DREAM CHECK
goal: Meaning builds worlds more quickly than we notice.
steps: 1. Take Event — Take one rigid reading of an event. Waking Dream — soften shoulders.
2. Compare Dream — Compare it with a dream: both organise fragments into a convincing world.
3. Identify Facts — Spot which facts are raw and which connections were constructed. Waking Dream — estimate odds.
4. Try Construction — Try one alternate construction and observe how lived experience changes. Waking Dream — next action.

title: RETURN THE PROJECTION TO SENDER
goal: The mind may be viewing its expectation on someone else’s screen.
steps: 1. Picture Quality — Picture the quality you are assigning outward. Return Projection — press feet.
2. Ask Internal — Ask what internal expectation, fear, or rule would make that quality especially visible.
3. Name External — Name the external evidence separately. Return Projection — notice detail.
4. Keep Facts — Keep what the facts support; return the excess meaning to your own inquiry. Return Projection — next action.

title: THE NO-JUDGEMENT OPTION STORM
goal: Evaluation kills possibilities before they are born.
steps: 1. Start Brief — Start a brief timer and generate options without ranking, explaining, or defending them. No Judgement — breathe naturally.
2. Include Conventional — Include one conventional, one tiny, one reversible, one collaborative, and one strange-but-safe possibility. No Judgement — notice detail.
3. Test Feasibility — Only after the timer ends may feasibility enter the room. No Judgement — next action.

title: THE AFTERSHOCK CLOCK
goal: Residual body alarm is not fresh evidence.
steps: 1. Set Reasonable — Set a reasonable after-event window during which shakiness, replay, fatigue, or emotion are expected echoes. Aftershock Clock — loosen hands.
2. Picture Time — Picture its end time.
3. Notice Sensations — Until then, Keep sensations but forbid them from changing your meaning of what happened. Aftershock Clock — name sensation.
4. Reassess — Reassess after recovery and sleep where possible. Aftershock Clock — next action.

title: LET THE IMAGE FIND ITS LAST FRAME
goal: Analysis may keep interrupting an unfinished inner sequence.
steps: 1. Bring Image — Bring up the image gently and prohibit verbal commentary. Let Image — move slowly.
2. Allow Move — Allow it to move at its own speed until it reaches a stable frame or natural ending.
3. Check Your Position — Notice whether your position, distance, or available action changes. Let Image — name sensation.
4. Use Sensory — Reorient afterward using present sensory facts. Let Image — next action.

title: CAPTURE THE MODEL’S MISS
goal: Reality’s surprise is premium evidence.
steps: 1. Keep Both Versions — The moment an outcome differs from expectation, Keep both versions verbatim. Capture Model — breathe naturally.
2. State Size — State the size and direction of the error.
3. Name Miss — Finish with: ‘The old model must now explain…’ and name the discrepancy. Capture Model — estimate odds.
4. Preserve Forecast — Do not let hindsight rewrite the original forecast. Capture Model — next action.

title: CONFIDENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE
goal: Certainty and support need separate meters.
steps: 1. Rate Sure — Rate how sure you feel from 0–100. Confidence Evidence — loosen hands.
2. Rate Evidence — Independently rate evidence quality using source reliability, directness, and recency.
3. Separate Meters — Picture the two scores on separate meters so certainty cannot masquerade as evidence. Confidence Evidence — pick action.
4. Follow Evidence — Let the evidence meter choose the action; treat the confidence meter as a feeling to notice, not a vote. Confidence Evidence — next action.

title: PUT AN EXPIRY DATE ON THE CONCLUSION
goal: Old evidence should not command new conditions forever.
steps: 1. Estimate Quickly — Estimate how quickly the conclusion’s evidence can become stale. Put Expiry — feel support.
2. Give Renewal — Give it a renewal date plus the data required then. Put Expiry — pick action.
3. Use Temporaryly — Until review, use it temporaryly; after expiry, it must be renewed by current evidence before influencing behaviour. Put Expiry — next action.

title: SAME FACTS, THREE ASSUMPTIONS
goal: Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.
steps: 1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed. Same Facts — press feet.
2. Reframe Three Ways — Run the same facts through three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the next action it recommends. Same Facts — find evidence.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions. Same Facts — next action.

1–2 minutes · Guided reset

GOAL
Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.

1. Keep Observations — Keep all observations fixed. Same Facts — press feet.
2. Reframe Three Ways — Run the same facts through three different assumptions about motive, capability, or context.
3. Identify Action — For each, spot the next action it recommends. Same Facts — find evidence.
4. Compare Action — Compare which action remains robust across versions. Same Facts — next action.

WIN
✓ Stress-test the belief by changing only its hidden premise.

Keep Observations → Reframe Three Ways → Identify Action → Compare Action

title: FIND THE MOVE NO FEELING MUST BETRAY
goal: Inner agreement is optional; a move that betrays no red line is enough.
steps: 1. Seat Feelings — Label up to three active emotions as players at the table. Leave them unnamed for the moment; observe first. Find Move — hear sound.
2. Vetoes — Give each emotion one veto: ‘Fear will not accept ___. Anger will not accept ___. Sadness will not accept ___.’
3. Clear Board — Cross out actions blocked by any safe, reasonable veto. Ignore demands for harm, punishment, or impossible certainty. Find Move — plain wording.
4. Choose Survivor — Choose one remaining action that crosses no red line, even if no feeling loves it. Find Move — next action.

title: POWER THEN, RESOURCES NOW

4. Find The Change — Notice what gives you more choice now.
5. Use One Resource — Pick one resource you have today and use it in one small action. Power Resources — next action.

2. Use Comparative — Use comparative language—cooler, warmer, neutral—rather than guessing degrees. Three Temperature — name sensation.
3. Let Readings — Let the three readings define the body’s current climate. Three Temperature — next action.

title: SCENT THE RETURN
goal: Train one neutral aroma to accompany successful orientation to the present setting.

2. Use After — Apply it only after you have genuinely returned to present time and choice.
3. Date Grounding — Pair it with date, place, and one grounding action across several occasions. Scent Return — notice detail.
4. Test Whether — Later, test whether the scent helps retrieve that state. Scent Return — next action.

3. Take Action — Do one thing you control, make one request where you have influence, and let go of one thing you can only watch. Three Rings — next action.

title: PLAY EMOTION JENGA
goal: Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.
steps: 1. Name Stack — Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental or your imagination block. Play Emotion — soften shoulders.
2. Pull One — Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Check Remainder — Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference. Play Emotion — name feeling.
4. Rebuild Stack — Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing. Play Emotion — next action.

title: OPEN THREE ENDING ROOMS
goal: The future should not be rehearsed as a single locked corridor.
steps: 1. Identify Critical — Spot the critical decision point in the dominant future scene. Open Three — widen gaze.
2. Create Endings — Create three endings by changing the choice there: cautious, courageous, and collaborative.
3. Cost — Notice the cost and value of each. Open Three — split duty.
4. Keep Best — Keep the ending that best fits evidence and values. Open Three — next action.

title: COMMON IS NOT THE SAME AS RIGHT
goal: Frequency cannot settle an ethical question.
steps: 1. State Social — State the social norm and your chosen criteria—harm, fairness, consent, dignity, responsibility. Common Same — soften shoulders.
2. Evaluate — Check the norm against each criterion without citing popularity. Common Same — add counterfact.
3. Keep Modify — Keep, modify, or reject it based on the ethical comparison. Common Same — next action.

title: RETURN THE SHAME TO ITS OLD ADDRESS
goal: A judging context can end while its standard keeps living inside you.
steps: 1. Identify Whose — Spot whose rule the shame is enforcing and the setting where it was learned. Return Shame — loosen hands.
2. Ask Whether — Check whether you still endorse that standard. Return Shame — split duty.
3. Keep Repair — Keep any ethical repair that is truly yours; return contempt, prejudice, or impossible expectation to its source. Return Shame — next action.
